title: Two members with the same PROGRAM-ID: a CALL resolves to the member named for the program, not its stale copy
realism: Estates keep backup members (PROG#OLD, PROGBKUP) made by copying a member under a new name without touching its PROGRAM-ID. Two source members then claim one program-name.
shapes: ORDV#OLD (member) holds PROGRAM-ID ORDVAL, a copy of ORDVAL taken before a change; ORDMAIN's CALL 'ORDVAL' resolves to ORDVAL.cbl
asserts: A dynamic CALL 'ORDVAL' loads the program object named ORDVAL, which is built from the member ORDVAL. The stale copy's PROGRAM-ID is a fact of its member, but no call resolves to it, and it is dead.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Programming Guide (SC27-8714-03)
citations.quote: The program-name in the PROGRAM-ID paragraph or ENTRY statement must be identical to the corresponding program object name or program object alias of the program object that contains the program.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: literal-1 or the contents of identifier-1 must specify the program-name of the called subprogram.

lower_confidence: IBM ties a dynamic call to the program object's name; that the object is linked under its source member's name is the standard compile-and-link procedure's convention, not a language rule. The key follows the convention every estate in the field ledger uses.

compile.reason: COPY ORDPRICE: the estate holds no copybook ORDPRICE (H-0053), so no compiler finds it
compile.check_note: a one-byte FILLER stands in for the missing COPY ORDPRICE

phantoms.why: apps/ORDR/cobol/ORDV#OLD.cbl holds PROGRAM-ID ORDVAL too, but CALL ORDVAL loads the program object built from apps/ORDR/cobol/ORDVAL.cbl

dead.name: ORDVAL
dead.why: a member copy whose PROGRAM-ID is still ORDVAL: CALL 'ORDVAL' loads the program object ORDVAL, never this member
